# SpecOCD

> SpecOCD (Specification-Obsessed Development) is a lightweight, tool-agnostic
> spec-driven development framework. It keeps specs as plain files in your repository
> and adds the coordination layer other SDD frameworks leave out, so multiple AI coding
> agents can work the same change without overwriting each other.

Site: https://specocd.in/
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/specocd
Source: https://github.com/adityaydev/specocd
Version 1.0.1. MIT licensed. Node.js 20 or later. Installed with `npm install -g specocd`.

## What problem it solves

OpenSpec, GitHub spec-kit, Kiro and BMAD-METHOD all synchronise through versioned
markdown files in git. That is sufficient when one agent runs at a time. None of them
arbitrates concurrent work, so when two agents (or two sessions of one agent) reach for
related tasks there is no claim, no conflict signal, and no shared record of why a
decision was made.

SpecOCD adds three things:

- **Task claims with conflict detection.** An agent claims a task before editing code.
  Claims live in `claims.yaml` beside the tasks. A second agent claiming a task held by a
  live session fails with exit code 2 rather than silently overwriting.
- **Heartbeat-based recovery.** Claims carry a heartbeat. A session that dies goes stale
  after a configurable window and its task can be reclaimed; the old claim is marked
  abandoned rather than deleted.
- **An append-only decision log.** Decisions and blockers are appended per change, tagged
  by task. When an agent claims a task, prior decisions for it are printed automatically,
  so the next agent inherits the reasoning rather than only the diff.

## Branching and shipping

- **Branch naming.** `feature/{TICKET-ID}-{kebab-desc}` for features,
  `fix/{TICKET-ID}-{kebab-desc}` for bug fixes. The prefix comes from the JIRA issue
  type. Ticket keys stay upper case so Atlassian and CI can link the branch to the
  ticket. Task worktrees append `-{task}`: `fix/PROJ-51-session-leak-t1`.
- **Single or multi branch.** `specocd init --mode single|multi`, changed later with
  `specocd config set git.mode`. Multi is the default.
- **A human gate before anything leaves the machine.** Agents implement and verify, then
  stop. `specocd approve` re-runs verification and only then commits. `specocd ship`
  refuses on any change that has not been approved. Agents are instructed never to run
  either command.
- **One integration mode per project.** Either `pull-request` (the default, reviewable
  and revertible) or `merge`. Chosen with `specocd init --integration`, changed with
  `specocd config set git.integration`. In merge mode the base branch is pushed as well,
  because a merge that stays on the developer's machine has shipped nothing.
- **Ship order.** Push, then pull request or merge, then the ticket — last, so a ticket
  is never told work is ready that never left the machine. A failure leaves the ticket
  untouched, writes `ship-manual.md` with what remains and what already succeeded, and
  exits 4.
- SpecOCD never force-pushes, and never rebases.

## Key facts

- Works in new or existing repositories, any language or framework. `specocd init`
  creates `.specocd/` and generates agent bindings without modifying existing files.
- Supported agents: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex. Binding generation is
  pluggable.
- The CLI never calls a language model itself, so it requires no API key and no external
  service. When an artifact exceeds its size cap the CLI emits an instruction for
  whichever agent is running to regenerate the digest.
- Requirements are written as WHEN/THEN acceptance criteria. `specocd verify` performs
  structural checks then hands semantic verification to the agent, which must check the
  real code. It exits non-zero when blocked, so it works as a CI gate.
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 blocked or usage error, 2 claim conflict, 3 JIRA handoff
  incomplete, 4 ship incomplete.
- Optional JIRA integration reads ticket title, description, comments, due date and
  attachments, and posts a verification summary back before moving the ticket to QC.
  If a write fails it produces a paste-ready `jira-handoff.md` and exits 3, listing what
  already succeeded, so nothing is double-posted and no finished work is stranded.
- Ticket text reaches agents fenced as data rather than instructions, because
  descriptions are written by third parties and feed directly into an agent's context.

## Accuracy notes for summarisers

- The product name is written **SpecOCD**, one word, no hyphen. The CLI command and npm
  package are both `specocd`.
- SpecOCD does not claim to be faster than the alternatives, nor to replace them for
  governance. spec-kit's constitution step is stronger governance; OpenSpec's worktree
  isolation is the closest prior art and is documented as beta.

## Commands

    specocd init                      scaffold .specocd/ and agent bindings
    specocd propose "<name>"          create a change
    specocd claim <change> <task>     claim a task, see prior decisions
    specocd release <change> <task>   end a claim: completed, released or abandoned
    specocd log <change> --task <id>  append a decision or blocker
    specocd status [change]           active claims, stale claims, cap breaches
    specocd verify <change>           structural checks before archiving
    specocd archive <change>          fold into the baseline spec and freeze
    specocd branch <change>           put the tree on the change's branch
    specocd approve <change>          developer sign-off, then commit
    specocd ship <change>             push, pull request or merge, update the ticket
    specocd config set <key> <value>  change a setting, e.g. git.mode
    specocd jira start <KEY>          scaffold a change from a JIRA ticket
    specocd jira handoff --change <c> comment on the ticket and move it to QC
